title: LMDB doesn't log 'IPNS unavailable' but SQLite and filesystem do — inconsistent and misleading
description: Scenario: operator reads startup logs after switching from Kubo to SQLite or filesystem backend. They see 'sqlite backend active — IPNS unavailable with this backend'. IPNS is a Kubo daemon concept, not a block store concept; this stoa is not an IPFS node and never offered IPNS to operators. The message will generate support questions ('what is IPNS?', 'how do I enable IPNS?'). LMDB backend logs nothing, making the inconsistency visible. The maintenance consequence: recurring support issue and false expectation. Fix: remove the IPNS warning entirely, or replace with a factual note ('Kubo IPNS publishing not available without kubo backend') only if the codebase actually had IPNS support at some point.
